liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (3 reviews): Jam builds from nothing to frenzy, then dissolves into Wharf Rat; Bird Song and the Jam into Wharf Rat are the main highlights [16][20][25]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song is noted as a worthy highlight of the performance [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-07-27.aud.sirmick.87464.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 14 songs; 98 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1973-07-27.aud.pantagruel.28882.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 14 songs; 96 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [2]
- **gd1973-07-27.mtx.seamons.100410.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 12 songs; 101 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [3]
- **gd73-07-27.aud.weiner.gdadt26.26363.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 12 songs; 91 min; rated 4.8/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is full, adds crowd reaction, and lacks harsh SBD cuts [23]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.weiner.180.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 90 min; rated 4.64/5 by 22 [9]. Said about its sound: Garcia's solo singing of "across the Rio Grande" is cut, losing the refrain; Jam sounds like Mountain pieces, with Phil's monster chord and Bobby's rhythm [15][22]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.miller.27779.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 89 min; rated 4.73/5 by 11 [10]. Said about its sound: Much better sounding than previous sources, though the Half-Step cut remains [20]

## Around the show

- Phil referred to the afternoon audience as a test, questioning their size [15]
- Crowds were unsanitary with full Mr. John's, mud, and heavy drug use [21]
- Lengthy Bird Song is close to, but not as good as, the 8/27/72 version [17]
- This Miller SBD is a nice upgrade over previous legendary Soundcheck sources [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-07-27.aud.sirmick.87464.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: aud (unknown gen) > ??? > wav > flac [1]. Also: DC offset removed, pitch corrected, dropouts repaired, remastered with iZotope Ozone and Waves Z-Noise [1]
- **gd1973-07-27.aud.pantagruel.28882.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Pantagruel; source: cassette (unknown gen) > HD [2]. Also: Cassette source is one generation less than the Audience Devotional Tree Round 26 principal source [2]
- **gd1973-07-27.mtx.seamons.100410.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [3]. Also: Transferred by Charlie Miller via Sony D8, RME Hammerfall, and Sony Vaio C1VP [3]
- **gd73-07-27.aud.weiner.gdadt26.26363.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [4]. Also: A>D by Noah Weiner using Nakamichi MR-1, Fostex D5, and Turtle Beach Montego II [4]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.weiner.180.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]. Also: Noah Weiner's source differed from this SBD, lacking some songs and text history [14]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.miller.27779.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [27]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [28]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [29]
- Poster by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1973-07-27 Fri Grand Prix Racecourse, Watkins Glen, NY](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1397163749719/grateful-dead-1973-07-27-fri-grand-prix) [30]
- Poster by gravitystereo: [Grateful Dead - Soundcheck '73 ( Flashback ) ( Grand Prix Racecourse , Watkins Glen , New York , July 27th , 1973 ) - gr](https://gravitystereo.com/product/grateful-dead-soundcheck-73-flashback-grand-prix-racecourse-watkins-glen-new-york-july-27th-1973/) [31]
